marks.gloss_en: the yevama is released by the yavam's death, a fortiori: a married woman, whose violation carries strangulation, is released by her husband's death; a yevama, bound by a mere prohibition, all the more so
the yevama is released by the death of the yavam (grounding the mishna's clause)
what of a married woman -- she also leaves by a get, which the yevama does not; the source case has an exit the target lacks
this one too leaves by a document -- she leaves by chalitza
for a married woman, the one who forbade her is the one who releases her -- the husband; here the man who forbade her (the deceased) is not the one whose death would release her
Rav Ashi: here too, the one who forbade her releases her -- it is the yavam who forbids her [while he lives], and the yavam['s death] that releases her
a married woman should leave by chalitza too: the yevama, who does not leave by get, leaves by chalitza; she who leaves by get, all the more so
'sefer kritut' -- a scroll severs her, and nothing else severs her
a married woman is not released by chalitza -- only the scroll severs her
a yevama should leave by get too: a married woman, who does not leave by chalitza, leaves by get; she who leaves by chalitza, all the more so
'vekatav LAH' -- for her, and not for a yevama
'beit chalutz haNa'al' -- released by the shoe yes, by anything else no
a yevama is not released by a get -- by the shoe yes, by anything else no
verbal designation should render the goat a sin offering, a fortiori from the case where the lottery does not sanctify
've'asahu chatat' -- the lottery renders it a sin offering, a verbal designation does not
chalitza is valid with anyone's shoe (the ribui), provided it fits him
